card.name: Common English words after degree adverbs
card.fires_on: Everyday English words such as current, new, poor, old and second, mostly right after a modifier like more, very, strong, totally or six tenths of a. It appears in general web text, not label text.

modes.label: Current after a modifier
modes.description: The word current follows a modifier, meaning either up-to-date or water flow.
modes.example: The version on-line will often be more<< current>> than the version available as a technical report

modes.label: Adjective after intensifier
modes.description: A short adjective such as poor, new or old follows an intensifier or a number word.
modes.example: The cards were very<< poor>> quality and many were reprints of earlier

modes.label: Unit or word part
modes.description: A time unit or a word part follows a fraction or hyphen.

card.plain: It marks plain everyday words like current, new or poor that come right after a modifier.
